Two Pointers.name: Two Pointers
Two Pointers.description: Maintain left and right pointers on the string to greedily check characters from ends.

Greedy.name: Greedy
Greedy.description: Making locally optimal choices at each step to find the global optimum, implemented here by starting from leaves and walking up to form paths.

Sliding Window.name: Sliding Window
Sliding Window.description: Technique for maintaining a window over an array to solve range queries, though typically restricted to arrays with non-negative numbers when finding sums.

Prefix Sum.name: Prefix Sum
Prefix Sum.description: Technique used to compute cumulative sums of an array in O(1) time after O(n) preprocessing, often combined with a hash map to find subarrays with a given sum.

Binary Search.name: Binary Search
Binary Search.description: Technique used to efficiently find the insertion position in the tails array for the non-decreasing subsequence.

Fenwick Tree.name: Fenwick Tree
Fenwick Tree.description: A data structure that supports point updates and prefix sum queries efficiently, often used for finding k-th elements using binary lifting.

Segment Tree.name: Segment Tree
Segment Tree.description: A binary tree used for storing intervals or segments, allowing answering range queries and point updates efficiently.
Segment Tree.time_complexity: O(n) build, O(log n) update and query

Dfs.name: Dfs
Dfs.description: Traversing tree structures by visiting nodes from leaves upwards to partition the tree into disjoint paths.

Dynamic Programming.name: Dynamic Programming
Dynamic Programming.description: Solving problems by breaking them down into simpler subproblems, often used here to find the longest increasing subsequence.

Bfs.name: Bfs
Bfs.description: Breadth-First Search on a binary tree to find the minimum changes/cost to reach any leaf node.

Grid Simulation.name: Grid Simulation
Grid Simulation.description: Iterating through grid cells and simulating local conditions based on neighbor values.

Sparse Table.name: Sparse Table
Sparse Table.description: Static Range Minimum Query data structure that can be used as an alternative approach for interval sizes.

relationships.detail: The solution combines two pointers with a greedy strategy to solve the problem.
Prefix sum with hash map handles negative numbers whereas sliding window generally does not for subarray sum problems.
Greedy simulation is used as the check function inside the binary search on the answer.
Binary search on the BIT is used within the Fenwick tree structure to find the k-th element.
Both data structures can handle range sum queries and point updates, though Segment Tree generalises to other operations.
Greedy tree traversal utilizes DFS-like bottom-up path construction to cover all nodes.
Binary search is used to optimize the inner lookup step of the LIS dynamic programming solution.
Segment tree is used to optimize the transition step of the dynamic programming solution.
Prefix sums are used inside the binary search condition to compute range sums in O(1).
Both can be used to solve the minimum interval query problem after sorting or coordinate compression.
Suffix sums are computed first to provide the values needed for the greedy decision at each step.

code_templates.explanation: Uses two pointers lo and hi to verify if the alphabetical characters from 'a' onwards appear at either end of the string.
Iterates from the largest digit 9 down to 1, greedily adding as much as possible to the remaining sum until the sum is satisfied.
Iterates through the string checking characters with an offset of 2 to count distinct pairs.
Uses a hash set and two pointers (lo and hi) to find the longest substring without repeating characters by sliding the window.
Uses a hash map frequency count and a variable-size sliding window with two pointers (lo and hi) to find the minimum window substring containing all characters of t.
Calculates the prefix sums of the bracket sequence to check if it's balanced and determines the minimum prefix sum to decide if 1 or 2 colorings are needed.
Uses a hash map to store the frequencies of prefix sums encountered so far, allowing us to find the number of valid subarrays ending at the current index that sum to k in O(1) time.
Implements binary search on the answer combined with a greedy check function to find the minimum feasible value.
Finds the leftmost position where target could be inserted while keeping the array sorted using standard lower bound binary search.
Standard Fenwick Tree implementation supporting point updates, prefix sum queries, and k-th element finding using binary lifting.
Standard Segment Tree implementation supporting point updates and range sum queries.
Precomputes prefix counts of 1s and suffix counts of 0s to efficiently calculate the change in inversions when flipping each element.
Iterates from each leaf node upward to the root to construct disjoint vertical paths using a visited array to prevent overlapping.
Iterates through the array and uses upper_bound to maintain a tails array of the smallest ending elements for non-decreasing subsequences of each length.
Uses BFS to traverse the tree while computing the minimum cost (changes required) to reach each node.
Simulates grid updates by checking each cell against its four neighbors and replacing it with the maximum neighbor value if it is strictly greater than all of them.
Segment tree supporting point updates and range maximum queries.
Sorts the array and builds a prefix sum array. For each element, uses binary search to find the furthest possible index that can be absorbed.
Sorts intervals and queries, then uses a priority queue to keep track of valid intervals covering the current query point.
Computes suffix sums from right to left, then greedily adds each positive suffix sum to the total answer since starting a new subarray there increases the sum.
